svg.aria-label: The unit cost, derived from the ceiling. Twelve dollars a month divided by roughly twenty-five to thirty thousand daily users comes to about four to five hundredths of a cent per daily user per month, or about forty-five cents per thousand daily users per month. A second line notes the experiment that established this cost sixty cents of generator time, once. The caption explains that this is the unit cost the chapter keeps asking for, that almost nobody computes it, and that it is what turns a capacity argument into arithmetic, since the same reasoning prices the upgrade ladder at twice the unit cost for twice the core.
